newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Lionore to bid for Forrestania.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Lionore to bid for Forrestania.

text.p: Forrestania Gold NL said on Monday it had received notice from Canadian mining group LionOre Mining International Ltd that it intends to make a cash and scrip takeover bid which valued Forrestania shares at A$3.35 each.

"Forrestania shareholders will have the opportunity to receive consideration of at least 50 percent cash and the balance in LionOre scrip, based on A$3.35 per Forrestania share or one LionOre share for each Forrestania share," Forrestania said, citing a letter from LionOre. LionOre shares closed at C$3.05 in Toronto on Friday.

Forrestania said it also planned to raise A$29 million through issues of shares and convertible notes to LionOre to pay for the A$20 million cash component needed to buy Normandy Mining Ltd's 62 percent stake in the Bounty mine in Western Australia.
The A$29 million capital raising includes an initial A$12 million from a placement of 4.8 million shares to LionOre at A$2.50 per share.
There would then be an issue of 4.7 million Forrestania shares to LionOre at A$2.50 per share to raise A$11.75 million.

LionOre had also agreed to subscribe for A$5.25 million of interest free, unsecured convertible loan notes, convertible into 2.1 million Forrestania shares at the option either of Forrestania or LionOre any time prior to June 30, 1998.

"The (takeover) bid will be conditional on Forrestania shareholders approving the placement and convertible note issue, acceptances being received that would increase LionOre's entitlement to at least 50.1 percent of Forrestania's issued capital and satisfactory financing arrangements being put in place to fund the cash components of the bid," Forrestania said.
LionOre's current four percent stake in Forrestania would increase to 19.8 percent after the share placements and 22.6 percent after the conversion of the convertible notes.
LionOre currently owns a 41.65 percent stake in Tati Nickel, a company with two producing nickel mines in Botswana.
Forrestania said it was poised to double its gold production to 150,000 ounces a year after the purchase from Normandy of the 62 percent of Bounty it does not already own.
The purchase price includes A$20 million cash, 5,000 ounces of gold a year, a five year unsecured A$6 million convertible loan note and a two percent gross royalty on nickel output.
